newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN DEFENCE FORCE SHRINKS, BLACKS DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN DEFENCE FORCE SHRINKS, BLACKS DOMINATE.

text.p: The South African National Defence Force has shrunk from 112,000 people in 1989 to 101,000 this year, but the number of permanent staff has more than doubled, officials said on Wednesday.

Defence department officials briefing members of parliament said the number of permanent force members had risen from 29,000 in 1989, when the country's defence relied mainly on low-paid white conscripts, to 75,000 at present.
The officials said the number of whites in the army, air force and navy had dropped from 73,000 or 66 percent in 1989 to 32,000 or 32 percent at present.

The democratic government elected in 1994 abandoned conscription almost immediately and launched a programme to integrate soldiers from former liberation movements, including President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress into a non-racial post-partheid defence force.

In a separate statement, the defence force said its members arrested 1,731 illegal immigrants during border patrols last month. It said this brought the total number of arrests since the beginning of the year to 30,474.
